# ColumnExplorer

<!-- Generated by scripts/sync-component-docs.mjs from ai/component-catalog.json and ai/component-composition.json. Do not edit; run `npm run catalog:sync`. -->

`@kerfjs/ui:column-explorer` · Kerf UI · component · Structure

A macOS-style column explorer for a hierarchy: one column of ListItem rows per level in a ColumnTrack, where choosing a row with children opens the next column; an optional preview column shows a chosen leaf. The application owns the nodes and the chosen path.

## When to use

Browse a large or deep hierarchy (files, categories, settings) one level per column, keeping the chosen path visible, with a paged layout for phones.

- People browse a deep hierarchy and benefit from seeing every level of the chosen path side by side: render ColumnExplorer with nodes (TreeList's TreeListNode) and path, set path to treeListPath(nodes, id) in the action handler, and wire wireColumnExplorer for the keyboard.
- The same hierarchy also shows as a TreeList: both read TreeListNode, so an app can switch between them.

**Not when:**

- Do not use it for a shallow hierarchy that fits one indented list; use TreeList.
- Do not build columns of Lists in a ColumnTrack by hand; use ColumnExplorer.
- Do not use it for a one-level-at-a-time flow with views and toolbars; use NavStack.

**Alternatives:**

- [TreeList](./tree-list.md) (nearest) — Use TreeList when the hierarchy reads best as one indented list.
- [NavStack](./nav-stack.md) (nearest) — Use NavStack when each level is a full view with its own toolbar.

## Imports

- JavaScript: `@kerfjs/ui/column-explorer` — exports `ColumnExplorer`, `ColumnExplorerProps`, `explorerColumns`, `explorerChosen`, `ExplorerColumn`.
- CSS: the browser build of `@kerfjs/ui/column-explorer` pulls its CSS automatically; import `@kerfjs/ui/column-explorer.css` manually only without the `browser` export condition.
- Wiring: `wireColumnExplorer` from `@kerfjs/ui/wire-column-explorer` (required).
- Declared side effects: browser-condition-css.

Exact prop names and types: [`@kerfjs/ui/column-explorer`](../public-api-signatures-v1.md#kerfjsuicolumn-explorer) in `public-api-signatures-v1.md`. Do not infer props from examples.

**Variants (configure, do not restyle):**

- scroll layout
- paged layout for phones

- disabled rows
- lazy children (hasChildren)
- compact density

## Composition

- Parents: any.
- Contexts: `application-ui`.
- Children: unrestricted.
- Built from: [ColumnTrack](./column-track.md), [List](./list.md), [ListItem](./list-item.md), [LucideIcon](./lucide-icon.md).

## State and wiring

**The app owns:** the nodes and loading their children; the chosen path (set it from action) and the preview content.

**Wiring:** `wireColumnExplorer` is required.

- Use wireColumnExplorer as documented.

## Geometry

Margin: child · border: child · padding: child (layout role: structure). `self` means the component already owns it — do not add wrapper padding, margin, or borders around it.

- ColumnTrack owns the sideways scroll and column widths; each column is a scrollable List of ListItem rows that own their insets. The explorer fills its parent's height.

## Accessibility

- The explorer is a region named by label; each column is a group named by its parent's label, and chosen rows carry aria-current. Rows that open a column show a chevron.
- With wireColumnExplorer: one Tab stop per column; Up and Down move, Home and End jump, Right opens a row's column and moves into it, Left returns to the column before, Enter and Space choose, and typing finds a row in the column.

## Styling boundary

The component owns its own styles. Configure it through its props and variants; do not override its internals.

Public class hooks (select for layout placement only, never to change the component's look): `kui-column-explorer`.

Never put `kui-column-explorer` on an element you write; render `ColumnExplorer` instead (`KUI-L103`).

Everything else is internal: `kerf-ui-analyze` reports private or unknown `.kui-*` selectors (`KUI-L001`, `KUI-L010`), unknown or private tokens (`KUI-L002`, `KUI-L012`), and any application rule that restyles the component, forced dimensions included (`KUI-L019`).
